standard_prerequisites.name: The union of cores and two-row tableaux
standard_prerequisites.statement: The target is the disjoint union over k of the matchings with short-chord-free core and the standard Young tableaux of shape (N-k,k).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the codomain in which the map F is asserted to be well defined.

standard_prerequisites.name: Core and two-row tableau of a matching
standard_prerequisites.statement: The core is the matching on the stable vertices and T(m) is the two-row tableau whose second row records the unstable chords.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two components of the map.

standard_prerequisites.name: Standard Young tableau
standard_prerequisites.statement: A two-row tableau of shape (N-k,k) is standard when both rows and both columns are increasing and each letter occurs once.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the property the proof verifies for T(m).

core_obligations: Use the well-definedness of the core and of the stable vertices to see that the two-row tableau T(m), whose second row collects the unstable chords, is well defined (source line 862).
Show that every letter of [N] occurs exactly once in T(m) and that its rows are increasing (source line 868).

Show that every entry of the second row is matched to a smaller entry in the first row, so that the columns are increasing and T(m) is standard, and note that the number of entries in the second row is the number k of unstable chords (source line 868).

proof_roadmap.step: Transfer well-definedness from the core and the stable vertices to the tableau, leaving standardness of shape to be checked.
Verify the standardness conditions and identify the size of the second row with the number of unstable chords.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled corollary at source lines 854-860: for nonnegative N and f the map F sending a matching in M_{N,f} to the pair consisting of its core and its two-row tableau is well defined. The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 861-869) first transfers well-definedness from the stable vertices and the core, and then has to check that the explicitly defined two-row tableau is standard: every letter occurs once, the rows increase, and each entry of the second row is matched to a smaller entry of the first row, which is what makes the columns increase; the count of unstable chords then identifies the shape. The statement records the map and none of the standardness verification.
